events.title: The founding of the Society of Jesus
events.shortBlurb: On the feast of the Assumption, Ignatius of Loyola and his companions bound themselves by vow at Montmartre…
body: Ignatius of Loyola, a Basque courtier whose leg was shattered by a cannonball at Pamplona in 1521, had been converted during his convalescence and schooled in prayer at Manresa. Studying at the University of Paris from 1528, he won six companions: Peter Faber of Savoy, Francis Xavier of Navarre, Diego Laínez, Alfonso Salmerón, Nicolás Bobadilla, and the Portuguese Simão Rodrigues.

On 15 August 1534, the feast of the Assumption, the seven climbed Montmartre and in a chapel bound themselves by vows of poverty and chastity and a promise to sail for Jerusalem to labor for souls; should that prove impossible, they would place themselves at the disposal of the pope. Faber, the only priest among them, offered the Mass at which the vow was made.

In 1537 they reunited at Venice, and when war with the Turks blocked their sailing, they were ordained priests and went to Rome. Pope Paul III approved their Company of Jesus in the bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae of 27 September 1540, and the companions elected Ignatius their first general. Within a generation the Society had become a force of education, mission, and reform.
